notes:
User feels overwhelmed by work and social commitments and wants to meet deadlines without burning out. They work 9–5 Monday–Friday and struggle to decline requests from colleagues and friends. They prefer a flexible, general planning approach rather than a strict schedule. Useful framework: identify daily must-dos, protect self-care, say no to nonessential commitments, communicate priorities, leave buffer time, and review tasks/commitments weekly. Their simple checklist includes: choose 3–5 daily must-dos, schedule meditation/journaling or other self-care, ask whether new commitments align with priorities, leave room for flexibility, and conduct a weekly review of priorities, commitments, and self-care. They found this checklist helpful, especially the weekly review.

trajectory:
User has trouble falling asleep despite journaling and a consistent sleep schedule, and is exploring additional sleep-quality strategies. They practice yoga and meditation as self-care, which has helped their anxiety and may also support sleep. They feel overwhelmed by commitments and are learning—with guidance from therapist Dr. Smith, whom they see every two weeks—to say no and set healthy boundaries without guilt or anxiety.

Current focus: discussing social commitments with their partner. Their partner often invites them to events, but user sometimes prefers staying home to relax. They plan to set limits on social commitments while preserving time together. They intend to use calm, empathetic “I” statements, listen actively, anticipate concerns, and handle resistance without becoming defensive. Useful guidance includes offering alternatives, reaffirming that boundaries support the relationship, and not treating the conversation as seeking permission. They are feeling ready to have the conversation and appreciate practical tips for staying calm, being firm, and following up afterward.
